34:T41e,The Next Web reported on 2026-07-21, and Bloomberg Law reported on 2026-07-20, that a federal court gave final approval to a US$1.5 billion settlement of the authors' copyright class action Bartz v. Anthropic, which concerned the downloading of pirated books used in model training. Other copyright suits against Anthropic appeared in search results but are not recorded here because they were not confirmed from fetched sources. CourtListener's index of US federal court dockets, searched on 2026-11-20, lists 75 dockets with Anthropic as a party. Cases filed against it since September 2026 include copyright suits by Reservoir Media Management (2026-10-21), ABG EPE IP LLC (2026-10-23) and Carlson LLC (2026-11-19) in the Northern District of California, an antitrust-coded case, Buist v. Anthropic (2026-09-18), a trademark case by Global Printing, Inc. dba MYTHOS in the Eastern District of Virginia (2026-11-13) and a patent case by Flinn Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Delaware (2026-11-12). The claims and their status were not reviewed.35:T680,The Associated Press reported on 2026-09-25 that the US Defense Secretary designated Anthropic a supply chain risk in February 2026, and that a federal appeals court in Washington ruled 2-1 that the Pentagon may keep the designation and bar Anthropic products from Defense Department work, including by contractors. Al Jazeera reported on 2026-08-28 that a federal district judge in California had ruled the designation unlawful, finding it followed Anthropic's public refusal to allow use of its models for domestic surveillance or autonomous weapons. AP reported that Anthropic said it disagreed with the appeals ruling and was considering further review, and that the ruling does not bar its products across the federal government. Il Sole 24 Ore reported on 2026-06-13 that Anthropic disabled its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for all customers three days after their launch, after receiving a US government directive on 2026-06-12, issued under export-control rules on national-security grounds, that required it to suspend access for foreign nationals; the report states that Anthropic said the action did not meet the standard of a transparent and fair process. The Regulatory Review reported on 2026-06-19 that the order came from the US Department of Commerce and cited a cybersecurity concern that Anthropic disputed; the two reports differ on whose access the order covered. Whether and when the restriction was lifted was not established in this search. 63:T680,The Associated Press reported on 2026-09-25 that the US Defense Secretary designated Anthropic a supply chain risk in February 2026, and that a federal appeals court in Washington ruled 2-1 that the Pentagon may keep the designation and bar Anthropic products from Defense Department work, including by contractors. Al Jazeera reported on 2026-08-28 that a federal district judge in California had ruled the designation unlawful, finding it followed Anthropic's public refusal to allow use of its models for domestic surveillance or autonomous weapons. AP reported that Anthropic said it disagreed with the appeals ruling and was considering further review, and that the ruling does not bar its products across the federal government. Il Sole 24 Ore reported on 2026-06-13 that Anthropic disabled its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models for all customers three days after their launch, after receiving a US government directive on 2026-06-12, issued under export-control rules on national-security grounds, that required it to suspend access for foreign nationals; the report states that Anthropic said the action did not meet the standard of a transparent and fair process. The Regulatory Review reported on 2026-06-19 that the order came from the US Department of Commerce and cited a cybersecurity concern that Anthropic disputed; the two reports differ on whose access the order covered. Whether and when the restriction was lifted was not established in this search. No enforcement action naming Anthropic was found in the FTC cases library, the SEC litigation releases and administrative proceedings lists, or the UK ICO enforcement list when searched on
